title.fa: هابز: بیماری‌هایی که دولت را از درون ویران می‌کند (لویاتان، فصل ۲۹)
title.en: Hobbes: the diseases that dissolve a commonwealth from within (Leviathan, ch. 29)
title.nl: Hobbes: the diseases that dissolve a commonwealth from within (Leviathan, ch. 29)

summary.fa: هابز فروپاشی درونی دولت را به بیماری تشبیه می‌کند و علت‌ها را می‌شمارد: قدرت ناکافی حاکم، شش عقیدهٔ فتنه‌انگیز (از جمله حاکمِ تابع قانون و تقسیم قدرت)، دو مرجع دینی و مدنی، انحصار، سردار محبوب و کشورگشایی. بخشی از این فهرست را سنت مشروطه‌خواهی وارونه کرده است.
summary.en: Hobbes likens internal collapse to disease and lists causes: insufficient sovereign power, six seditious doctrines (including a ruler under law and divided power), rival spiritual and civil authorities, monopolies, the popular general and conquest. Constitutionalism has inverted part of this list.
summary.nl: Hobbes likens internal collapse of the state to disease and lists its causes.

text.fa: هابز می‌گوید دولتی که از درون فرو می‌پاشد قربانی «تأسیس نادرست» است، نه سرشت مردمش: تقصیر با آدمیان در مقام سازنده است، نه در مقام مصالح ساختمان. خانه‌ای که بدون معمارِ توانا ساخته شود بر سر فرزندان خراب می‌شود (ص ۲۹۲).
text.en: Hobbes says a commonwealth that dissolves from within is a victim of 'imperfect institution', not of its people's nature: the fault lies with men as makers, not as matter. A house built without an able architect falls on the heads of posterity (p. 292).
text.nl: Hobbes says a commonwealth that dissolves from within is a victim of 'imperfect institution', not of its people's nature: the fault lies with men as makers, not as matter. A house built without an able architect falls on the heads of posterity (p. 292).

text.fa: بیماری نخست: حاکمی که برای رسیدن به قدرت به اختیاری کمتر از آنچه صلح و دفاع لازم دارد رضایت دهد. وقتی بعداً بخواهد آن را پس بگیرد، مخالفانش از دولت‌های خارجی کمک می‌گیرند، که هیچ فرصتی را برای تضعیف همسایه از دست نمی‌دهند. نمونه‌هایش بکت و پاپ در برابر هنری دوم، و بارون‌ها و فرانسویان در برابر شاه جان است (ص ۲۹۲–۲۹۳).
text.en: First disease: a ruler who, to obtain power, settles for less authority than peace and defence require. When he later tries to resume it, his opponents get help from foreign states, which never miss a chance to weaken a neighbour. His cases: Becket and the Pope against Henry II, the barons and the French against King John (pp. 292–293).
text.nl: First disease: a ruler who, to obtain power, settles for less authority than peace and defence require. When he later tries to resume it, his opponents get help from foreign states, which never miss a chance to weaken a neighbour. His cases: Becket and the Pope against Henry II, the barons and the French against King John (pp. 292–293).

text.fa: سپس شش «عقیدهٔ فتنه‌انگیز» را می‌شمارد: هر کس خود داور نیک و بد باشد؛ عمل برخلاف وجدان شخصی همیشه گناه باشد؛ ایمان از الهام مستقیم بیاید نه آموزش؛ حاکم تابع قانون مدنی باشد؛ مالکیت افراد در برابر حاکم مطلق باشد؛ و قدرت حاکمه تقسیم‌پذیر باشد (ص ۲۹۳–۲۹۵).
text.en: He then lists six 'seditious doctrines': that each person is judge of good and evil; that acting against private conscience is always sin; that faith comes by direct inspiration, not teaching; that the sovereign is subject to civil law; that subjects' property is absolute against the sovereign; and that sovereign power may be divided (pp. 293–295).
text.nl: He then lists six 'seditious doctrines': that each person is judge of good and evil; that acting against private conscience is always sin; that faith comes by direct inspiration, not teaching; that the sovereign is subject to civil law; that subjects' property is absolute against the sovereign; and that sovereign power may be divided (pp. 293–295).

text.fa: استدلالش علیه «حاکمِ تابع قانون» پس‌رویِ بی‌پایان است: اگر قانون بالای حاکم باشد داوری هم بالای او لازم است که مجازاتش کند، و آن داور حاکم دوم است که خودش داور سومی می‌خواهد. دربارهٔ تقسیم قدرت هم می‌گوید قدرت‌های تقسیم‌شده یکدیگر را نابود می‌کنند (ص ۲۹۵).
text.en: His argument against a sovereign under law is an infinite regress: if law stands above the sovereign, a judge above him is needed to punish him, and that judge is a second sovereign needing a third. On division he says divided powers mutually destroy each other (p. 295).
text.nl: His argument against a sovereign under law is an infinite regress: if law stands above the sovereign, a judge above him is needed to punish him, and that judge is a second sovereign needing a third. On division he says divided powers mutually destroy each other (p. 295).

text.fa: دو قدرت در یک کشور: وقتی مرجع دینی حق تعیین گناه دارد و دولت حق تعیین قانون، هر تبعه دو سرور دارد و «مملکتی که تجزیه شده روی پای خود نمی‌ایستد». هابز می‌گوید ترس از تاریکی و ارواح از هر ترس دیگری قوی‌تر است و همین به قدرت روحانی توان برهم زدن دولت می‌دهد؛ این را به صرع تشبیه می‌کند (ص ۲۹۷–۲۹۸).
text.en: Two powers in one country: when a religious authority claims to define sin and the state to define law, every subject has two masters and 'a kingdom divided cannot stand'. Hobbes says fear of darkness and spirits is stronger than any other fear, which gives the spiritual power its capacity to disturb the state; he likens it to epilepsy (pp. 297–298).
text.nl: Two powers in one country: when a religious authority claims to define sin and the state to define law, every subject has two masters and 'a kingdom divided cannot stand'. Hobbes says fear of darkness and spirits is stronger than any other fear, which gives the spiritual power its capacity to disturb the state; he likens it to epilepsy (pp. 297–298).

text.fa: «حکومت مرکب»: اگر مالیات دست مجمع، فرماندهی دست یک شخص و قانون‌گذاری وابسته به توافق آن دو باشد، به نظر هابز این یک دولت نیست بلکه سه جناح مستقل است (ص ۲۹۸–۲۹۹).
text.en: 'Mixed government': if taxation lies with an assembly, command with one person, and legislation depends on their agreement, for Hobbes this is not one commonwealth but three independent factions (pp. 298–299).
text.nl: 'Mixed government': if taxation lies with an assembly, command with one person, and legislation depends on their agreement, for Hobbes this is not one commonwealth but three independent factions (pp. 298–299).

text.fa: بیماری‌های کوچک‌تر: دشواری گردآوری پول برای نیازهای دولت؛ انباشته شدن خزانه در دست چند نفر از راه انحصار؛ محبوبیت شهروندِ جاه‌طلبی که سپاه را شیفتهٔ خود می‌کند (نمونه‌اش سزار) و به گفتهٔ هابز در حکومت مردمی خطرناک‌تر است؛ شهرهای بیش از حد بزرگ و انجمن‌های بسیار، «دولت‌های کوچک در شکم دولت بزرگ»؛ و اشتهای سیری‌ناپذیر برای گسترش قلمرو (ص ۲۹۹–۳۰۱).
text.en: Lesser diseases: difficulty raising money for the state's needs; treasure pooling in a few hands through monopolies; the popularity of an ambitious subject who wins the army (Caesar), more dangerous, Hobbes says, in popular government; over-great towns and many corporations, 'lesser commonwealths in the bowels of a greater'; and the insatiable appetite for enlarging dominion (pp. 299–301).
text.nl: Lesser diseases: difficulty raising money for the state's needs; treasure pooling in a few hands through monopolies; the popularity of an ambitious subject who wins the army (Caesar), more dangerous, Hobbes says, in popular government; over-great towns and many corporations, 'lesser commonwealths in the bowels of a greater'; and the insatiable appetite for enlarging dominion (pp. 299–301).

text.fa: انحلال: وقتی دشمن در جنگ خارجی یا داخلی پیروز نهایی شود و دولت دیگر نتواند از اتباع حمایت کند، تکلیف اطاعت پایان می‌یابد و هر کس آزاد است حمایت را هر جا می‌یابد بجوید (ص ۳۰۱).
text.en: Dissolution: when an enemy wins final victory in foreign or civil war and the state can no longer protect its subjects, the duty of obedience ends and each is free to seek protection wherever he finds it (p. 301).
text.nl: Dissolution: when an enemy wins final victory in foreign or civil war and the state can no longer protect its subjects, the duty of obedience ends and each is free to seek protection wherever he finds it (p. 301).

text.fa: هابز تقلید از همسایگان و خواندن تاریخ یونان و روم را هم سبب شورش می‌داند و می‌خواهد این کتاب‌ها بدون «اصلاح استادان» در دسترس همگان نباشد، چون کشتن شاه را با نام «جبّارکشی» ستودنی می‌کنند (ص ۲۹۵–۲۹۷).
text.en: Hobbes also blames imitation of neighbours and the reading of Greek and Roman histories for rebellion, and wants such books not publicly read without 'correctives of discreet masters', since they make king-killing laudable under the name of tyrannicide (pp. 295–297).
text.nl: Hobbes also blames imitation of neighbours and the reading of Greek and Roman histories for rebellion, and wants such books not publicly read without 'correctives of discreet masters', since they make king-killing laudable under the name of tyrannicide (pp. 295–297).

text.fa: سنجش: سنت مشروطه‌خواهی (لاک، مونتسکیو، قانون اساسی آمریکا) درست وارونهٔ سه مورد از این فهرست را پایهٔ آزادی می‌داند: حاکمِ تابع قانون، تفکیک قوا و مالکیت مصون از دولت. تجربهٔ سه سدهٔ بعد نشان داد دولتِ دارای قدرت تقسیم‌شده می‌تواند پایدار بماند، و پژوهش نهادی امروز تمرکز قدرتِ بی‌مهار را سرچشمهٔ شکست می‌داند. در مقابل، هشدارهای هابز دربارهٔ دو مرجع قانون‌گذار، انحصار، سردارِ محبوب و دخالت خارجی در شکاف داخلی هنوز جدی گرفته می‌شود. این بند از ویراستار است.
text.en: Assessment: the constitutionalist tradition (Locke, Montesquieu, the US constitution) makes the exact opposite of three items on this list the basis of liberty: a ruler under law, separation of powers, and property secure against the state. Three centuries showed that states with divided power can be stable, and current institutional research sees unchecked concentration as a source of failure. By contrast Hobbes's warnings about two law-giving authorities, monopolies, the popular general and foreign meddling in domestic rifts are still taken seriously. This paragraph is the editor's.
text.nl: Assessment: the constitutionalist tradition (Locke, Montesquieu, the US constitution) makes the exact opposite of three items on this list the basis of liberty: a ruler under law, separation of powers, and property secure against the state. Three centuries showed that states with divided power can be stable, and current institutional research sees unchecked concentration as a source of failure. By contrast Hobbes's warnings about two law-giving authorities, monopolies, the popular general and foreign meddling in domestic rifts are still taken seriously. This paragraph is the editor's.
